notes.calculus-section-13-4-19: Speed squared=8(t−4)²+153; its global minimum occurs at t=4.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-20: Newton’s law gives F=m r″ for constant mass m.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-21: The stated applied net force is(0,0,20)N and mass4kg, so acceleration is(0,0,5)m/s²; integrate with the initial data.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-22: Constant speed means v·v is constant, not necessarily v itself.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-23: Use g=9.8m/s², no drag, equal launch/landing heights; horizontal speed is constant.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-24: Solve100+v_y t−gt²/2=0 for the positive flight time. Impact kinetic energy includes the initial100m elevation.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-26: The two elevations are complementary because they have the same sin(2θ).
notes.calculus-section-13-4-27: At the apex vertical speed is zero; use g=32ft/s² and sin36°.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-29: For ground impact inside the city require y(100)>15 and range<600; y(100)>15 already implies range>100. Wall-grazing/boundary endpoints are excluded.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-30: The apex time is v0 sinα/g and maximum height is(v0 sinα)²/(2g).
notes.calculus-section-13-4-31: Vertical motion80t−16t² gives positive landing time5s; x=50t,y=−2t².
notes.calculus-section-13-4-32: Axes east,north,up give a=(5,0,−9.8); initial velocity(0,−15√3,15). Use positive time30/9.8.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-33: dy/dx=(f(x)−5sinθ)/(5cosθ). Zero net drift requires5sinθ=mean(f)=2m/s. The S-shaped drift is consistent with slow banks and fast central water.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-34: Mean current is(1/40)∫0^40 3sin(πx/40)dx=6/π; cancel it with the southward component of boat velocity.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-35: r·(c×r)=0 and c·(c×r)=0; their derivatives show constant radius and axial coordinate. If c×r0=0 the point is stationary.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-36: On a fixed line both derivatives follow its direction; constant speed gives v·a=0.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-37: aT=(v·a)/|v| is signed; aN=|v×a|/|v| is nonnegative, at regular points.

notes.calculus-section-13-4-43: The diagram suggests an angle of roughly60° between a and the forward tangent: aT≈10cos60°,aN≈10sin60°. The drawing is not an exact angle specification.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-44: Use the cross-product product rule and v×v=0.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-45: At t=1, r=(4,2,5),r′=(1,1,2). Adding2r′ gives the station(6,4,9). The tangent must meet all three station coordinates.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-46: Integrate dv=v_e dm/m for constant relative exhaust vector. A speed gain2|v_e| requires m_final/m_initial=e^−2.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-1-project-kepler-s: The polar cross product gives h=r×r′; a small sector has area½r²dθ.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-2-project-kepler-s: Areaπab divided by areal rateh/2 gives T; substitute h²=GMb²/a.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-3-project-kepler-s: Kepler’s law solves for semimajor axis a; the requested major-axis length is2a. Convert days to seconds.
notes.calculus-section-13-4-4-project-kepler-s: Use T=24h as the exercise approximation, compute orbital radius(GMT²/4π²)^(1/3), then subtract Earth radius. Using a sidereal day differs by about77km and is accepted.
